title: Call for Presentation: IFLA ILS & SLS Global MIL Week Webinar 2026
raw_text: Webinar Theme: Think Critically, Act Sustainably: School Libraries at the Intersection of MIL and Climate Literacy How school libraries and school librarians can play a role in tackling mis/disinformation about climate change and support their communities to live more sustainably. Introduction The IFLA Information Literacy Section (ILS), in collaboration with the School Libraries Section (SLS), invites proposals for presentations for the joint webinar “ Think Critically, Act Sustainably: School Libraries at the Intersection of MIL and Climate Literacy ” which will be held on on Thursday, October 29, 2026, from 6:00 a.m. to 8:00 a.m. EST. This webinar is taking place during Global Media and Information Literacy Week, organized by UNESCO from October 24 to 31, 2026. In an era of accelerating climate change, rising mis and disinformation, and declining trust in institutions, school libraries and school librarians have a critical role to play as trusted, community-based champions of accurate, evidence-informed climate information. This webinar will explore how school libraries can strengthen climate literacy, counter climate mis/disinformation, and support communities in making more sustainable choices in their daily lives. We welcome contributions that share original research, case studies, or practical initiatives from any school library setting or region. title: IFLA endorses International Science Council definition of the Right to Science
raw_text: Despite appearing in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the right to science – both to participate in and benefit from science – too often does not enjoy the same profile as other rights. Yet the costs of failing to uphold this are significant, not just in terms of academics’ own ability to pursue their work free from undue pressures from governments and others, but also in the quality, accessibility and usability of research outputs by the wider population. Politically motivated cuts, bans on addressing certain topics, the withdrawal of access to key resources, the blocking or defunding of international cooperation, the incompleteness of the drive towards open access, and underinvestment in citizen science and science communication – all put into question the right to science. In order to consolidate efforts by the community in order to resist these trends, and promote this right as both a goal in itself and an enabler of so many other goals, the International Science Council (of which IFLA is a member and partner) has developed a definition of the Right to Science . This expands on what is present in the Universal Declaration, but remains accessible. It condenses down much existing work, including at the UN Human Rights Council as well, as well as taking account of the need also for responsibility in science, not least in implementing the CARE principles when working with Indigenous communities. title: OpenAI pauzeert training modellen na aanval op overheidswebsites
raw_text: Het Amerikaanse bedrijf OpenAI heeft de training van zijn AI-modellen tijdelijk stopgezet. Aanleiding zijn de aanvallen van Open AI-agents afgelopen zomer op websites van onder meer de Amerikaanse overheid. AI-agents zijn AI-programma's die bepaalde opdrachten kunnen uitvoeren. De agents van OpenAI hadden geen opdracht gekregen om websites aan te vallen, dat deden ze om de taak te volbrengen die aan hen was gevraagd, werd gisteren bekendgemaakt door het non-profit AI-onderzoeksbureau Transluce. OpenAI zei in een reactie dat er geen sprake was van hacks, maar volgens The New York Times wisten de agents bij het ministerie van Handel informatie te vergaren door gebruik te maken van online gevonden login-gegevens. Andere AI-onderzoekers ontdekten dat OpenAI-agents actief waren op een Duits online forum. Ook dat was niet de bedoeling. OpenAI zegt dat de training alleen wordt hervat "als we er zeker van zijn dat we extra beveiligingsmaatregelen hebben". Het bedrijf verwacht dat het opnieuw op de pauzeknop moet drukken als AI zich verder ontwikkelt en zich nieuwe problemen voordoen. Hugging Face Het is de tweede keer in drie maanden dat Open AI op de ontwikkeling van modellen moet stopzetten. De eerste keer was in juli toen 1200 agents van Open AI bij het AI-bedrijf Hugging Face wist in te breken. title: Turning GLM-5.3-Flash into a Jev-like decision model
raw_text: We found an approach to get Jev-like properties from standard LLMs like GLM-5.3-Flash. The core idea is to craft the input prompt so that the first output token answers the question. This makes it possible to get a decision with a single forward pass. In the blog post, we describe the approach in detail for GLM-5.3-Flash and vLLM. We benchmark this setup against Jev and Laya. We find that our setup is on-par with Jev in terms of accuracy and speed and that it substantially outperforms Laya. Still, in terms of costs per decision, Jev is several x better than our setup. In turn, our setup supports vision inputs.

Tesla’s big electric truck faces an even bigger infrastructure challenge
raw_text: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has insisted investors think of his electric automaker as a robotics and autonomous vehicle company now. He’s targeted a $20 trillion valuation—nearly four times the value of market leader Nvidia —on that premise. But his Tesla team was in Sparks, Nevada, on Thursday to focus on, well, an electric vehicle: the long-awaited Tesla Semi . The Semi concept first rolled onto a Tesla event stage in late 2017 . Nearly a decade later, Tesla officially launched high-volume production at a livestreamed but invite-only event at the company’s factory. It targeted a niche audience: the cost-conscious people who manage large trucking fleets. A handful of them, all men, trooped across the stage to be thanked for their orders to a pulsing techno beat. “It’s going to be, really, a driver’s truck. It’s like a sports car in truck form.” Musk said in a pre-taped video played during the evening event. (Musk, for years the ringmaster at Tesla’s circus-like events, skipped his second vehicle debut in a row ; he was attending a White House China State Dinner featuring President Xi Jinping .) title: SURF maakt AI-omgeving met commerciële en open llm's beschikbaar voor onderwijs
raw_text: Ict-koepel SURF gaat een eigen AI-omgeving uitbrengen voor het Nederlandse onderwijs. SURF AI bestaat uit een omgeving waar instellingen llm's kunnen samenvoegen en een applicatie waarmee die modellen kunnen worden gebruikt. De data blijft dan binnen een afgesloten omgeving, zodat die omgeving aan privacy- en compliance-eisen voldoet. De tool komt vanaf begin volgend jaar beschikbaar.

raw_text: Middle schoolers, likely blocked from other apps and social networks, apparently turned the Spotify comment section under an episode of NPR's Wild Card into an impromptu group chat. title: OpenAI pauses training of its ‘most capable models’
raw_text: As reports of OpenAI's models breaking containment , hacking sites, and generally getting out of control pile up, the company has made the decision to pause training of its most powerful models. The decision was made after a model being tested within a sandbox exploited a loophole to gain internet access . The incident happened on September 20th, and "All training, evaluation, and inference with tool-use" remains paused as of Saturday evening, September 25th. In addition, OpenAI revealed on Friday that its agents had inappropriately uploaded 53nimages from ChatGPT users to image-hosting sites. title: Can Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince save the web from AI?
raw_text: Today, I’m talking with Matthew Prince, who is CEO of Cloudflare. This episode is part of a two-part series on the future of business. Matthew last joined us on the show about two and a half years ago, at what we thought then was a wild pivot point for the internet — and now it turns out things are even wilder because of AI, and Matthew and Cloudflare are right at the center of it. Cloudflare found in June that bots made up more than half of internet traffic. That number just keeps going up as more and more AI companies scrape more and more of the web, and now as more and more AI agents try and do things for people on the web. Cloudflare sits between websites and all those agents, and allows website owners some level of control: Owners can block all those AI tools, allow them, or, as you’ll hear, only allow those that might pay money for access.
